output.answer:
To trace a custom agent, use the Agents tracing APIs: `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()` and `start_tool()`. To keep follow-ups together, reuse one stable `conversation_id`. For bad answers, create a custom tag signal in the Agents tab's Signals UI. The docs I read describe creating it in the UI, not in code.

**1. Trace the agent**
- Install `weave` and call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_*` call. Without `init`, the tracing functions silently do nothing [S3].
- A conversation groups turns, a turn is one user-agent exchange, and a turn contains LLM calls and tool calls [S1].
- Use the context-manager form. The span closes and is sent at the end of the block, even after an exception. Nested calls can find their parent through context [S7].

**2. Keep follow-ups in one conversation**
- `start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on every child span so turns group in the Agents tab. A supplied ID must stay stable for the conversation's lifetime. Reusing it adds new turns to that conversation. If you omit it, the SDK generates a UUID [S5].
- A turn created with no active conversation has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped [S6].
- Tracing doesn't replace message history. Your agent still has to keep the dialogue and send it to the model on each turn.

```python
import weave
from weave.conversation import Message

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

def call_model(history):          # placeholder: your LLM client call
    return "..."

history = []                      # your retained user + assistant messages
CONVERSATION_ID = "my-conversation-abc"   # store this per user session

def handle_user_message(text):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
    with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent",
                                  conversation_id=CONVERSATION_ID) as conv:
        with conv.start_turn(user_message=text):
            with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o", provider_name="openai") as llm:
                answer = call_model(history)
                llm.input_messages = [Message(role=m["role"], content=m["content"]) for m in history]
                llm.output_messages = [Message(role="assistant", content=answer)]
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": answer})
    return answer
```

This is a minimal sketch. I haven't run it, and `call_model` is a placeholder. It follows the documented `start_conversation`, `start_turn` and `start_llm` patterns [S5][S7][S8]. Add `weave.start_tool(...)` inside an LLM block if your agent calls tools [S7].

**3. Add a custom Signal for bad answers**
1. In Forge, open your project, click **Agents**, then the **Signals** tab. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal**, then **Custom Signal** [S2].
2. Fill in these fields [S2]:
   - **Tag name**: the label shown in the Agents view, for example "bad-answer".
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior. An LLM judge scores each turn and applies the tag when the turn matches. For bad answers, you would describe what counts as one, such as incorrect or unhelpful responses. This wording is my example, not the docs'.
   - **Scorer name** and **Inference model or custom runtime**. Serverless Inference is the default and uses CoreWeave Forge credits.
   - Optional under **Advanced**: include tool calls, filter which turns are scored, and set a sample rate.
3. Click **Create signal**. Weave then scores matching turns, and the tag appears in the Agents view [S2].

Tags only show rows for spans that matched at least one tag. A signal can run successfully and still show no output [S9].

**Limits of my research:** I didn't read the "Start a tool call" section or the manual `.end()` pattern in detail. I also didn't find a code-based way to define custom signals.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

### Error signals

Error signals categorize failed traces by root cause to help you identify and resolve infrastructure and application issues.

| Signal | What it detects |
| - | - |
| **Network Error** | DNS failures, timeouts, connection resets, and other connectivity issues |
| **Ratelimited** | HTTP `429` responses, quota exhaustion, and throttling from upstream APIs |
| **Request Too Large** | Requests exceeding size or token limits, such as context window exceeded |
| **Bad Request** | Client-side errors where the server rejected the request (`4xx` except `429`) |

| **Bug** | Flaws in application code such as `KeyError`, `TypeError`, or logic errors |

   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

To trace a custom agent, use the Agents tracing APIs: `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()` and `start_tool()`. To keep follow-ups together, reuse one stable `conversation_id`. For bad answers, create a custom tag signal in the Agents tab's Signals UI. The docs I read describe creating it in the UI, not in code.

**1. Trace the agent**
- Install `weave` and call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_*` call. Without `init`, the tracing functions silently do nothing [S3].
- A conversation groups turns, a turn is one user-agent exchange, and a turn contains LLM calls and tool calls [S1].
- Use the context-manager form. The span closes and is sent at the end of the block, even after an exception. Nested calls can find their parent through context [S7].

**2. Keep follow-ups in one conversation**
- `start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on every child span so turns group in the Agents tab. A supplied ID must stay stable for the conversation's lifetime. Reusing it adds new turns to that conversation. If you omit it, the SDK generates a UUID [S5].
- A turn created with no active conversation has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped [S6].
- Tracing doesn't replace message history. Your agent still has to keep the dialogue and send it to the model on each turn.

```python
import weave
from weave.conversation import Message

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

def call_model(history):          # placeholder: your LLM client call
    return "..."

history = []                      # your retained user + assistant messages
CONVERSATION_ID = "my-conversation-abc"   # store this per user session

def handle_user_message(text):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
    with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent",
                                  conversation_id=CONVERSATION_ID) as conv:
        with conv.start_turn(user_message=text):
            with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o", provider_name="openai") as llm:
                answer = call_model(history)
                llm.input_messages = [Message(role=m["role"], content=m["content"]) for m in history]
                llm.output_messages = [Message(role="assistant", content=answer)]
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": answer})
    return answer
```

This is a minimal sketch. I haven't run it, and `call_model` is a placeholder. It follows the documented `start_conversation`, `start_turn` and `start_llm` patterns [S5][S7][S8]. Add `weave.start_tool(...)` inside an LLM block if your agent calls tools [S7].

**3. Add a custom Signal for bad answers**
1. In Forge, open your project, click **Agents**, then the **Signals** tab. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal**, then **Custom Signal** [S2].
2. Fill in these fields [S2]:
   - **Tag name**: the label shown in the Agents view, for example "bad-answer".
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior. An LLM judge scores each turn and applies the tag when the turn matches. For bad answers, you would describe what counts as one, such as incorrect or unhelpful responses. This wording is my example, not the docs'.
   - **Scorer name** and **Inference model or custom runtime**. Serverless Inference is the default and uses CoreWeave Forge credits.
   - Optional under **Advanced**: include tool calls, filter which turns are scored, and set a sample rate.
3. Click **Create signal**. Weave then scores matching turns, and the tag appears in the Agents view [S2].

Tags only show rows for spans that matched at least one tag. A signal can run successfully and still show no output [S9].

**Limits of my research:** I didn't read the "Start a tool call" section or the manual `.end()` pattern in detail. I also didn't find a code-based way to define custom signals.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

sources.text:
## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

### Error signals

Error signals categorize failed traces by root cause to help you identify and resolve infrastructure and application issues.

| Signal | What it detects |
| - | - |
| **Network Error** | DNS failures, timeouts, connection resets, and other connectivity issues |
| **Ratelimited** | HTTP `429` responses, quota exhaustion, and throttling from upstream APIs |
| **Request Too Large** | Requests exceeding size or token limits, such as context window exceeded |
| **Bad Request** | Client-side errors where the server rejected the request (`4xx` except `429`) |
| **Bad Response** | Invalid, unexpected, or unusable responses from remote services (`5xx`) |
| **Bug** | Flaws in application code such as `KeyError`, `TypeError`, or logic errors |

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

To trace a custom agent, use the Agents tracing APIs: `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()`, `start_llm()` and `start_tool()`. To keep follow-ups together, reuse one stable `conversation_id`. For bad answers, create a custom tag signal in the Agents tab's Signals UI. The docs I read describe creating it in the UI, not in code.

**1. Trace the agent**
- Install `weave` and call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_*` call. Without `init`, the tracing functions silently do nothing [S3].
- A conversation groups turns, a turn is one user-agent exchange, and a turn contains LLM calls and tool calls [S1].
- Use the context-manager form. The span closes and is sent at the end of the block, even after an exception. Nested calls can find their parent through context [S7].

**2. Keep follow-ups in one conversation**
- `start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on every child span so turns group in the Agents tab. A supplied ID must stay stable for the conversation's lifetime. Reusing it adds new turns to that conversation. If you omit it, the SDK generates a UUID [S5].
- A turn created with no active conversation has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped [S6].
- Tracing doesn't replace message history. Your agent still has to keep the dialogue and send it to the model on each turn.

```python
import weave
from weave.conversation import Message

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

def call_model(history):          # placeholder: your LLM client call
    return "..."

history = []                      # your retained user + assistant messages
CONVERSATION_ID = "my-conversation-abc"   # store this per user session

def handle_user_message(text):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
    with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent",
                                  conversation_id=CONVERSATION_ID) as conv:
        with conv.start_turn(user_message=text):
            with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o", provider_name="openai") as llm:
                answer = call_model(history)
                llm.input_messages = [Message(role=m["role"], content=m["content"]) for m in history]
                llm.output_messages = [Message(role="assistant", content=answer)]
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": answer})
    return answer
```

This is a minimal sketch. I haven't run it, and `call_model` is a placeholder. It follows the documented `start_conversation`, `start_turn` and `start_llm` patterns [S5][S7][S8]. Add `weave.start_tool(...)` inside an LLM block if your agent calls tools [S7].

**3. Add a custom Signal for bad answers**
1. In Forge, open your project, click **Agents**, then the **Signals** tab. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal**, then **Custom Signal** [S2].
2. Fill in these fields [S2]:
   - **Tag name**: the label shown in the Agents view, for example "bad-answer".
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior. An LLM judge scores each turn and applies the tag when the turn matches. For bad answers, you would describe what counts as one, such as incorrect or unhelpful responses. This wording is my example, not the docs'.
   - **Scorer name** and **Inference model or custom runtime**. Serverless Inference is the default and uses CoreWeave Forge credits.
   - Optional under **Advanced**: include tool calls, filter which turns are scored, and set a sample rate.
3. Click **Create signal**. Weave then scores matching turns, and the tag appears in the Agents view [S2].

Tags only show rows for spans that matched at least one tag. A signal can run successfully and still show no output [S9].

**Limits of my research:** I didn't read the "Start a tool call" section or the manual `.end()` pattern in detail. I also didn't find a code-based way to define custom signals.
